He finds it easiest to concentrate at night, when the Hungarian capital gradually falls silent. Olah has taped foil and cardboard over the tiled floor at the back of the gallery. Pots of brushes, tubes of paint, pencil sketches, and, over and over again, pictures that include the blue-and-green Roma flag line the room. Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. stories.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
stories.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MZxq Some researchers argue that artificial general intelligence could pose unforeseeable risks Image: Marc Asensio/NurPhoto/IMAGO Advertisement Dramatic warnings about the existential risks posed by artificial intelligence to humanity are nothing new. As early as the 1940s, the renowned scientist and science fiction author Isaac Asimov explored potential risks and unintended consequences of intelligent machines. In 1991, Hollywood blockbuster "Terminator 2" imagined a dystopian 2029 in which an out-of-control military AI called Skynet directs killer robots in a war against humanity. If the warnings of several of the biggest names in AI are to be believed, a similar scenario could become a reality — even before 2029.
